subject: model
value: The extracted plain-text body of one cataloged PDF, stored once per document.
justification: The DDL makes doc_id both PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY to documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE: the row is a 1:1 extension of a document holding its extracted body, and doc_id identifies it in every legal state. The single open subject, text, is unique across 43 rows only by accident - it is one archived document body, not an identifier, and nothing in the schema or extractor forbids two documents yielding the same text. The MANIFEST records exactly the case that would break it: `1-s2.0-S037704271000645X-main.pdf` is the 'Published Elsevier (2011) version of 09root - same paper, different typesetting'; a re-typeset or re-extracted duplicate can collide. text is one value that happens to be long (an archived body), so it is atomic; it is not offered as an atomicity subject. Scope is current-state: the blob is a derivative of the bytes at documents.path produced by the last extraction run, so doc_id -> text is true of this snapshot and of this extractor, not invariantly - re-running pdftotext, or replacing the PDF, rewrites the text under the same doc_id.

subject: author
justification: 6 rows / 36 columns; `author` has 5 distinct values, so almost every group is a singleton. The one repeat (ids 2 and 3, 'Mark Gillespie, Denise Yang, Mario Botsch, Keenan Crane') is the same paper plus its own supplement, which is why producer/publication_year/topic appear constant per author. An author does not own a PDF toolchain string, a year, or a topic label: any second unrelated paper by the same author breaks all three at once. The remaining part, author -> inferred_author, is not an entity FD but a builder copy: author IS inferred_author in 6/6 rows precisely because author_source='agent-read' in 6/6 rows (verified: sum(author IS inferred_author)=6, sum(author_source='agent-read')=6). Normalizing on it would yield a table keyed by an author string whose only payload is the same author string. `documents` is a per-PDF-file catalogue keyed by path/id (its declared intended_keys), not a person registry.

subject: inferred_author
justification: Mirror image of the `author` candidate and accidental for the same reasons. inferred_author -> author is the same builder copy (the two columns are byte-identical in all 6 rows under author_source='agent-read'), not ownership. inferred_author -> producer / publication_year / topic holds only because the sole repeated value spans ids 2 and 3, the Gillespie et al. paper and its supplement, which naturally share pdfTeX-1.40.24, 2024, and harmonic-implicit-tracing. The agent's inferred spelling of a name identifies nothing in the modelled world; the document does.

subject: original_author,topic
justification: A composite of a mostly-empty raw metadata field and a category label, which is exactly the shape that collides rarely in a 6-row table. original_author is the empty string in 4 of 6 rows. Ids 5 and 6 both sit in the group ('', 'non-euclidean-rendering') and coincidentally both publish in 2022 (Coulon et al. and Novello et al. are unrelated works). The dependency survives only because id 1 happens to be the one row whose pdfinfo carried an author ('Laszlo Szirmay-Kalos'); had that PDF's metadata been empty like the other four, ('', 'non-euclidean-rendering') would map to both 2021 and 2022 and the FD would fail immediately. It is contingent on PDF-extraction luck, not on domain structure. Neither a raw author string nor a topic tag owns a publication year.

subject: original_title
justification: Killed outright by id 5: original_title='Ray-Marching Thurston Geometries' with original_author='' (pdfinfo_ok=1, pdfinfo_error=''). That row proves the two raw pdfinfo fields go missing independently, so the uniform ''->'' group formed by ids 3, 4 and 6 is coincidence rather than structure; a PDF with a title but no author already exists in this very table, and the reverse would break the dependency. Outside that sentinel group the 3 non-empty titles are simply unique across 6 rows. Both columns are peer attributes scraped from the same PDF's metadata block; a raw title string is not an entity that owns an author.

subject: producer
justification: `producer` is a PDF-generation toolchain string ('Acrobat Distiller 10.1.8 (Windows)', 'pdfTeX-1.40.24', 'cairo 1.18.4', 'xdvipdfmx (20210318)', and '' for id 5) - bookkeeping about how the file was rendered, identifying nothing about the work. Its only repeated value, pdfTeX-1.40.24, spans ids 2 and 3, which are the same paper and its supplement; that single accident is what makes author, inferred_author, publication_year and topic all look constant per producer. Any second unrelated pdfTeX-built paper in the corpus - overwhelmingly likely in a real bibliography - breaks all four dependencies simultaneously. Approving this would create a 'producer' entity owning authorship and subject matter.

subject: publication_year
justification: A year is a scalar bookkeeping value and cannot own a subject classification. With only 4 distinct years over 6 rows the groups barely have a chance to conflict: 1996 and 2021 are singletons; 2024 covers ids 2 and 3, the same paper plus its supplement; and 2022 covers ids 5 and 6, two unrelated works (Coulon et al., Novello et al.) that merely happen to carry the same topic label 'non-euclidean-rendering'. Note also that 2021 and 2022 already map to the same topic, so the relation is nowhere near injective - one differently classified 2022 paper ends it. topic is assigned per document by the routing pass (see MANIFEST.md), not derived from the year.

subject: model
value: One PDF currently held in the SurfLab collection, with its on-disk facts (path, size, hash, page count), its extracted/inferred bibliographic metadata, and the naming decision applied to it.
justification: The DDL declares id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE; both are coherent - path is the collection-relative location of one PDF, id the intake surrogate used by every FK (document_text, methods, rankings). The 23 open uniqueness subjects are 43-row accidents. sha256 gets a non-unique index while duplicate_sets(sha256 PRIMARY KEY, count, paths_json) exists precisely to record one hash at several paths, so the author expects hash collisions. filename, suggested_name and standard_filename equal each other in all 43 rows and path = suggested_folder||'/'||suggested_name, so their uniqueness is just path's uniqueness inside a single folder; source_subgroup exists so nested subgroups may later repeat a basename. size_bytes, text_chars, pages+venue, author+venue, title, inferred_title, what_it_does and original_path are measurements or curated prose that nothing forbids two papers sharing. The BCNF violations from [author, creation_date, producer] are Ghostscript/pdfTeX metadata artefacts of 43 curated rows. Scope is current-state: one row per file presently on disk, and path -> sha256/size_bytes/text_chars holds only of this scan - replacing a PDF in place changes the hash under the same path.

The DDL declares id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE; both are coherent - path is the collection-relative location of one PDF, id the intake surrogate used by every FK (document_text, methods, rankings). The 23 open uniqueness subjects are 43-row accidents. sha256 gets a non-unique index while duplicate_sets(sha256 PRIMARY KEY, count, paths_json) exists precisely to record one hash at several paths, so the author expects hash collisions. filename, suggested_name and standard_filename equal each other in all 43 rows and path = suggested_folder||'/'||suggested_name, so their uniqueness is just path's uniqueness inside a single folder; source_subgroup exists so nested subgroups may later repeat a basename. size_bytes, text_chars, pages+venue, author+venue, title, inferred_title, what_it_does and original_path are measurements or curated prose that nothing forbids two papers sharing. Scope is current-state: one row per file presently on disk, and path -> sha256/size_bytes/text_chars holds only of this scan - replacing a PDF in place changes the hash under the same path.

subject: model
value: One content hash that the last intake scan found at more than one path in the collection, together with how many paths carry it and the list of those paths.
justification: The DDL declares sha256 TEXT PRIMARY KEY, which is coherent: the relation is a GROUP BY sha256 HAVING count(*)>1 aggregate over documents, so the hash is the grouping value and identifies the row. count and paths_json are both functions of that group. The table is empty only because the present 43 documents have 43 distinct hashes; that is evidence about the current corpus, not about the intended key, and the DDL settles the key without rows. Scope is per-build: the relation holds no authored content of its own and nothing in it survives a rebuild - it is recomputed wholesale from documents.sha256 by each intake scan, and MANIFEST.md lists it with the other generated artefacts (FTS5 index, v_rankings, v_methods, manifest.json). paths_json is a serialised list of the several paths carrying one hash, i.e. several instances of one fact, and would normalise to duplicate_path(sha256, path); no atomicity subject was raised for it because the table has zero rows to profile.

subject: name
justification: The DDL comments name as 'the novel method/equation name' - singular. The flagged example, 'c=(1-t0^2)/(1+t0^2), s=2t0/(1+t0^2), q_j=2t_j/(1+sum t_i^2)', is one rational parameterisation whose commas separate the coordinate components of a single mathematical object, exactly like the sibling row '<f,g>_L2 = int_0^1 f g dt = <B^n b, B^n c>_E = sum b_i c_i'. It is one long structured value, not a list of several methods; a second method from the same paper gets its own row with the next seq.

subject: locator
justification: `locator` is free text a human wrote to point into a paper ('Eq. (32), line ~839', 'Section 7 vertex-shader listing (line ~1122)'), and it is near-unique: 21 distinct values across 22 rows. It determines `kind` for the trivial reason that 20 of its 21 groups are singletons. The table contains its own counterexample: 'Sections 2, 3.2, 4' has kind='method' while 'Section 2 / 3.2' has kind='equation' - near-identical locator text, opposite kind - showing the string carries no information about what is being located. The one genuine collision, 'Section 4' at ids 1 and 9, is two different documents (doc_id 1 and doc_id 2) that both happen to point at a method. The column is also declared NOT NULL DEFAULT '', so the moment any two methods are recorded without a locator, the empty-string group collides across both kinds. The real owner here is the declared key (doc_id, seq): a method entry belongs to a document at a position, and both `kind` and `locator` are attributes of that entry.

subject: model
value: One novel method, equation, algorithm, formula or concept curated out of one paper, at its ordinal position within that paper's extraction, with where it appears and how it maps to the project's render code.
justification: id is the declared PRIMARY KEY. (doc_id, seq) is a genuine second identity, not a 180-row coincidence: seq runs exactly 1..n within every document with no gaps or repeats, v_methods orders by it, and the DDL comments describe one extracted item per row - the ordinal of an extraction inside a paper identifies that extraction in every legal state. name and description are curated prose, unique today only because 43 papers were read once; the MANIFEST itself records a same-paper-twice pair (09root and its Elsevier reprint 1-s2.0-...), which would yield identical method names and descriptions, so both are accidental. kind is a five-value enumeration and locator a section reference, so the reported 'name -> kind' and 'description -> locator' transitive dependencies are artefacts of those columns being unique. links is empty in all 180 rows, producing the spurious constant-column 2NF finding. Scope is current-state: methods carries no portable identity of its own - doc_id points at documents.id, an intake-assigned rowid, so (doc_id, seq) identifies a row only within this snapshot's id assignment and would not survive a rebuild of the inventory.

subject: model
value: The project's applicability judgement of one cataloged document - its score, tier, the reason for it, and a document-level note on how it links to the render code.
justification: The DDL declares doc_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY, so exactly one applicability ranking exists per document and doc_id identifies it. The single open subject, reason, is a paragraph of curated justification: unique across 43 rows today, but nothing forbids two off-theme papers receiving the same sentence, and the reported reason -> score/tier/links dependencies follow only from that accidental uniqueness. I checked the MANIFEST's tier legend as a possible real derivation and it fails: score=2 maps to both off-theme and conceptual-seed, so tier is an independent curated judgement, not a band of score. links here, unlike methods.links, is genuinely populated. The scope column is constant 'applicability' with a DEFAULT; it anticipates further ranking lenses, and if a second lens is ever stored the key must become (doc_id, scope) - but the declared PK is coherent for today's intent and I take it as declared. Scope is current-state: doc_id is documents' intake-assigned rowid, so the key does not survive an inventory rebuild, and the MANIFEST shows scores being revised in place with no history kept.
